label: real local service with upstream stand-in providers — never real generation, never product acceptance
ffmpegVersion: ffmpeg version 8.1.2 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers

assertions.description: prepare-runtime.sh verify mode reports verified:true
init-instance created a fresh instance
instance.json exists after init-instance
BUDGET.md exists after init-instance
init-instance is idempotent on rerun
submit outcome is accepted
a brand-new submit is not replayed

scenarios.name: S2 exact replay of the same prepared bytes -> replayed=true, same runId

assertions.description: an exact replay reports replayed:true
an exact replay reports the same runId

scenarios.name: S3 same requestId, different body -> 409 conflict

assertions.description: the server refuses a same-id different-body submit as conflict (409)

value.detail: this requestId was already used with different content

scenarios.name: S4 server-side invalid body (422) + client-local unsupported planVaryOn refusal

assertions.description: a schema-invalid body (narration < 4 sentences) is rejected 422
the 422 refusal reason is invalid
assertions.detail: {"contractVersion":1,"outcome":"refused","requestId":"wave1-proof-complete-video-protocol-2026-09-19T20-32-25-145Z-invalid","reason":"invalid","detail":"narration: Too small: expected array to have >=4 items"}

assertions.description: prepareCutroomRequest rejects planVaryOn:'angle' locally, before any HTTP call

body.detail: narration: Too small: expected array to have >=4 items

scenarios.name: S5 lost response, reconciled by requestId, then a genuine replay

assertions.description: a genuinely lost response surfaces as a transport_error
the lost POST is reported write-uncertain
the proxy dropped exactly the one armed connection
the later exact replay reports replayed:true
the replay names the same runId the lookup found
exactly one run row exists for this requestId

observations: the server genuinely processed the lost submit: runId 16c71c39-dd82-4f2d-a955-a2660dc58ba6 exists for requestId wave1-proof-complete-video-protocol-2026-09-19T20-32-25-145Z-lost-response

scenarios.name: S6 lookup of an absent requestId -> 404

assertions.description: a lookup for an unused requestId is not_found

observations: this is a current observation only: absence now does not certify absence later

scenarios.name: S7 complete video run

assertions.description: strict cursor paging reached run.finished with continuous seqs
result is completed/video with a contained, ffprobe-readable video

observations: 3 stills all contained in the instance artifact root

streams.codec_long_name: H.264 / AVC / MPEG-4 AVC / MPEG-4 part 10

scenarios.name: S8 graceful restart mid-run, resumed by a reconstructed caller

assertions.description: at least one event was observed before restarting
worker1 reports {"stopped":true} on SIGTERM
api1 reports {"stopped":true} on SIGTERM
the run is genuinely still running when both processes stopped
api2 restarted on the exact same port
the reconstructed caller process exits 0
the reconstructed caller resumed at least one event
after restart the run reaches completed/video with a contained, ffprobe-readable video

observations: 14 pre-restart events observed before stopping (cursor 14), after a 900ms interrupt budget
jobs after graceful stop: reel.plan=done, reel.keyframes=done, reel.clips=done, reel.assemble=queued
14 pre-restart + 27 post-restart events, seq-continuous with no regression or duplication

scenarios.name: S9 crash: SIGKILL worker and api, restart, and reclaim the abandoned job

assertions.description: worker1 holds at model call 12 (shot 0's reconcile call)
worker1 was actually killed by SIGKILL
api1 was actually killed by SIGKILL
api2 restarted on the exact same port
after the crash+restart the run completed a video with a contained, ffprobe-readable file
the full event history (across the api restart) is seq-continuous with no gaps or duplicates
reel.clips was reclaimed and run a second time

observations: using recommendedLeaseMs=1000 from phase 1's upstream-validated restart fixture

scenarios.name: S10 cancel with no worker, then observe what starting one produces

assertions.description: with no worker started, the run is running before cancel
cancel() returns a schema-valid RunStatus (per the contract)

observations: state after starting a worker post-cancel (15s window): finished

actual terminal result upstream produced after a cancel with no worker, then a worker started: {"contractVersion":1,"runId":"1da09b4f-10bd-4f6c-866a-3be9da9f53f3","requestId":"wave1-proof-cancel-2026-09-19T20-32-25-145Z","costCents":0,"status":"cancelled"}
